findings.text: follow-on: the search guard asserts source.count('responses.get(') == 1, so it catches an inline lookup only when spelled that way. A genuine bypass written as response = (record.get('responses') or {}).get(str(finding.get('id'))) in review_scope leaves the count at 1 and passes this assertion; I applied that exact mutation and only test_review_scope_shows_the_accessors_reason reddened (1 failed 28 passed EXIT=1). The sentinel tests still hold the three named readers, but the count assertion does not establish the done-when's 'one function' claim against an arbitrary spelling.

follow-on: routing review_scope through _stored_response changes two narrow behaviours of the prior inline code — the finding id is now stripped before lookup (was str(finding.get('id')) unstripped) and a non-Mapping responses value now yields None where the old responses.get would raise. Both are the plan's intended unified rule and are inert for well-formed records, but neither divergence is exercised by a test, so a record with a whitespace-padded id would resolve differently than before with nothing asserting which is correct.

follow-on: the reviewed manifest declares no baseline_suite or after_suite arm (its test_logs name the head gate, the negative control and a bare new-test run), so the store's added-failure derivation reads unmeasured (null) rather than a measured zero; recording the two arms would let a later reader derive the delta this one-arm evidence cannot.

justifications.evidence: I re-ran the declared gate at head ddd2f02647 in a scratch extraction of the reviewed tree (reviewer-head-gate.log, 29 passed EXIT=0, module.__file__ under the scratch root) and reproduced both negative-control arms (reviewer-negative-control.log, 2 failed 27 passed EXIT=1, the same two ids the reviewed run's own negative_control.log names; reviewer-negative-control-folds.log, 2 failed 2 passed EXIT=1); it is 19 rather than 20 because the reviewed manifest arms no baseline_suite/after_suite, so the store's added-failure derivation is unmeasured (null) rather than a measured zero.
justifications.fit: the added name describes mechanism (_stored_response) and its docstring states the invariant (an answer is keyed in responses by the finding's stripped id; a record with no responses map, a finding with no id, or an id with no entry has no stored response) rather than the change history, with no version, plan, sprint or ticket identifier and no attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the §9(e) deliverable is met point for point: plan_review.py:1307 is the one function that looks a finding's stored response up by its id (the search the node runs returns one line), and declined_recurrence (plan_review.py:1445), _acted_finding_types (plan_review.py:1601) and review_scope (plan_review.py:1240) each read response = _stored_response(record, finding); the gate re-run at head is 29 passed EXIT=0 with the existing tests of all three unchanged, and each reader follows the patched accessor — declined_recurrence counts a declined finding, the fold counts an acted one, review_scope shows the sentinel reason.
justifications.reuse: the change is itself the de-duplication the review of the recurrence-fold node asked for — the per-finding response lookup that declined_recurrence, _acted_finding_types and review_scope each carried is now held once — and it reuses the module's existing stripped-id keying (finding_ids) and Mapping guards rather than introducing a new reader.
